He did not speak for himself, did not build his own position, did not draw disciples to follow him; he did only one thing: pointing to the Christ who was coming.
Jesus said, “He has testified to the truth.” This shows that truth is not a set of doctrines; truth is a person, Jesus.
John's mission was not to enlighten but to identify; not to create light but to lead people to the true Light.
2. Jesus points out: His identity needs no human testimony (verse 34)
Jesus said, “But the testimony which I receive isn't from man.”
He meant: I am not established by human testimony, not by human affirmation, not by human approval; I am by nature truth, by nature have authority, and by nature come from the Father.
Jesus did not need people to testify for Him, because the Father had already testified for Him (as discussed in the previous passage).
Then why did He mention John? He said, “that you may be saved.”
In other words: it was not that He needed John's witness, but that people needed someone to guide them to Jesus so that they might be saved.
John's witness was for people, not for Jesus; to turn people back, not to have Jesus affirmed.
3. John was a lamp, but people were only willing to rejoice in his light for a while (verse 35)
“He was the burning and shining lamp, and you were willing to rejoice for a while in his light.”
These words carry deep sorrow.
1. John was “the burning lamp”
He was the one who prepared the way for Jesus; his light was a witness from heaven; he lit the darkness, guided hearts, and called to repentance.
But note that Jesus called him “a lamp,” not “the true light.”
The true Light is Jesus (John 1:9).
John was the lamp, Jesus is the Light; the lamp points to the light, the light brings out life.
2. People “rejoiced for a while” in his light
This is Jesus' heartache. People liked John's courage, message, fervor, and call, but only “for a while.”
They admired John but did not accept the Lord he pointed to. They loved to hear the cry of repentance but would not truly repent. They were drawn to John but unwilling to walk toward Jesus.
They could clap, be stirred, and discuss, but were unwilling to have their lives changed.
This is also the condition of many people toward truth today: liking inspiration but not obeying; liking the light but not walking into it; liking to hear a calling but not truly responding.
Here Jesus reminds us: true salvation is not admiring the witness, but walking toward the One to whom the witness points.
4. What this passage reminds us
1. The witness of truth is meant to lead people to Jesus, not to leave them at liking a spiritual feeling.
2. Jesus' identity does not rely on human testimony; He Himself is truth.
3. People easily like spiritual light but are unwilling to actually repent.
4. When the true Light has come, we need to open ourselves to Him, not stop at admiring the message.
q: Do you sometimes stop at “liking the light” without truly walking toward the light of Jesus?
Which call from Him today do you need to answer for real?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for raising up witnesses to guide us toward the true Light, Jesus Christ. Keep us not only liking the light but truly walking toward it; not only moved by the call but willing to repent. May our hearts be fully open to You as we follow Your Son, Jesus. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: But the testimony which I have is greater than that of John, for the works which the Father gave me to accomplish, the very works that I do, testify about me, that the Father has sent me.
b: This verse is Jesus' confirmation once more of His identity, and it unveils the deepest meaning of all His work on earth. He does not prove Himself by words, nor by human recommendation, but by the “works” the Father entrusted to Him, showing that He is the Christ.
Jesus said His witness was greater than John's, because His witness does not come from man but from the Father, brought out by “completing the Father's mission.”
This verse shows us three profound truths:
1. Jesus' witness is greater than John the Baptist's
John the Baptist is called the greatest of the prophets, the greatest “among those born of women” (Matthew 11:11). But Jesus said: My witness is greater than his.
Why? Because John's witness “pointed” to Jesus, while Jesus' witness “accomplished” the Father's work.
John prepared the way; Jesus is the way itself.
John was the lamp; Jesus is the Light.
John called for repentance; Jesus forgives sins.
John pointed out the Lamb; Jesus is the Lamb.
So His witness is naturally deeper, greater, and truer than any human witness.
2. The work the Father gave is Jesus' witness
Jesus said, “For the works which the Father gave me to accomplish, the very works that I do.”
He meant: every single thing I do is what the Father told me to do; every single thing I accomplish is what the Father wanted me to accomplish.
This includes:
• healing the paralytic
• washing away iniquity
• proclaiming the kingdom of heaven
• giving eternal life
• calling disciples
• healing the blind
• raising the dead
• going to the cross
• rising from the dead
None of these was an itinerary Jesus arranged Himself; they were the Father's plan being fulfilled step by step in Him.
Jesus' work did not come from His own ideas, but from the Father's heart.
Everything He did was a concrete expression of the Father's voice; every step He took was a concrete fulfillment of the Father's will.
He did not live for Himself but for the Father; He did not act on His own but by the Father.
This is the meaning of His saying, “the works which the Father gave me to accomplish.”
3. Jesus' work itself is the Father's testimony to Him
“These very works that I do, testify about me, that the Father has sent me.”
In other words: His actions are His identity; His miracles are His evidence; His works are His proof; all that He accomplished is the Father's seal upon Him.
The Father did not need to recommend Him in words, because His works already proved that He came from the Father.

The paralytic rising is the Father's witness; the blind seeing is the Father's witness; sinners forgiven is the Father's witness; the dead raised is the Father's witness; His own resurrection from the dead is the Father's last and highest witness.
Jesus did not need anyone to make up for Him; His work itself is His seal.
For Jesus, what mattered most was not how people evaluated Him but how the Father affirmed Him. He did not seek the applause of men, only the completion of the Father's will.
This is His life, and also His example.
q: Today, what do you care about most: “how people see me” or “how the Father sees me”?
Are you willing, like Jesus, to focus on completing the Father's will rather than seeking people's applause?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for testifying to us through all that Jesus did, proving that He is the Holy One You sent. Let us learn from Jesus not to seek people's evaluation but to seek Your will; not to follow our own thoughts but to obey Your heart. May our lives also become part of Your work, so that the world may see You. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
